key_insight: Using an LLM as a feature-extraction interface, rather than the final diagnostic engine, produced more reliable pediatric appendicitis prediction than end-to-end LLM diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This hybrid design could make narrative clinical notes easier to use in decision support while reducing missed appendicitis cases in pediatric triage.
method: LLM extracts schema-constrained clinical features from free-text narratives
Deterministic plausibility checks validate extracted features
Validated features are fed into an XGBoost classifier trained on clinical, lab, and ultrasound data
evidence_signal: The system was tested on two independent pediatric appendicitis cohorts from German hospitals and compared with open-source and proprietary LLM baselines, including narrative reordering robustness checks.
watch_item: The approach still depends on accurate feature extraction and validated local integration, so performance may shift if note styles, templates, or hospital workflows differ.
paper_title: Language Models as Interfaces, Not Oracles: A Hybrid LLM-ML System for Pediatric Appendicitis
